notes: VECTOR exception: craters.bin is little-endian Float32 triples [latDeg, lonDeg, diameterKm], sorted largest first, not a Uint16 raster. Use craters.json LOD prefix counts. Robbins circular-fit columns LAT_CIRC_IMG, LON_CIRC_IMG, DIAM_CIRC_IMG. Keep diameter >=5 km globally OR centre latitude <=-75 degrees and diameter >=1 km. Longitude wrapped to [-180,180). Public-domain NASA PDS numerical data (PDS Geosciences FAQ, https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/faq.html); no access or use constraints in the product FGDC metadata. No separate Creative Commons licence is asserted. Credit Stuart J. Robbins / Southwest Research Institute and USGS Astrogeology Science Center. The separate craters-small-south.bin contains both archived CSVs; licence CC BY 4.0; credit Marco Figuera et al. (2022) and Zenodo 5779260. It is a limited study area, not a complete south-pole survey or a map of ice. All archived small rows retained, including rows outside the paper's final 200-1000 m filtered analysis sample.

title: Permanent shadow
shortHelp: Blue patches never get direct sunlight. Darker blue means more of that square is in shadow. These are cold traps where ice could last; this is not a map of measured ice.

Credit NASA/GSFC/LOLA team. No NASA endorsement is implied. Exact area-weighted averages of native20m pixels (no COG overviews):4096PNG alpha=round(200*fraction), 2048BIN raw=round(10000*fraction), decode raw*0.01 percent. Native source uses the same sphere, pole, axes,20m cell edges and608km extent as the app. Outside80S is nodata65535/transparent. Cell fractions use the full map-plane cell area, with source nodata contributing zero; pixel centres decide the80S mask. This2023 adjusted terrain model differs from the old2016 240m map, especially at small shadows. Majority-shadow agreement with ice.bin=99.298%; PSR intersection-over-union=89.751%.

title: Where water ice may be
shortHelp: Blue: ice predicted just under the ground. Cyan: predicted surface cold traps. White is for measured signs from orbit, but no white pixels are available. Only the Cabeus marker shows a direct water measurement.
units: class: 0 none mapped; 1 predicted buried; 2 predicted surface; 3 orbital detection

source.version: PRP V2.0 (2018-02-21), existing MOONDA temp-max linear grid; PGDA LOLA 20m PSR

notes: Prediction, not an inventory or proof of ice. Class 1: nearest PRP triangle-centre ice_depth >0 and <=1 m, and existing annual maximum surface temperature >=110 K. The PRP depth corresponds to 1 kg/m²/Ga sublimation loss; invalid -999 depths are retained and never interpolated away. Class 2: the cell contains >0% 20m-source permanent shadow and annual maximum surface temperature <110 K (Paige2010 approximate long-term stability threshold). A class-2 cell can contain unshadowed ground; only its mapped PSR portion is coloured in the 4096 PNG. Class 3 is reserved and empty: Li2018 point coordinates are available upon request, and the public Lemelin2021 polygons give counts rather than detection coordinates. Do not fill those polygons or crater circles with detected ice. No direct-confirmation raster class exists; Cabeus LCROSS confirmation is a marker restricted to its measured impact plume. 0 means none mapped under these rules, not proven absence. Source thermal model is about 0.5km and not sharpened by 4096 display. Sources: data-raw/pds-diviner-prp/dlre_prp_south.zip member dlre_prp_south.tab; dlre_prp.fmt; app/public/data/layers/temp-max.bin; features/downloads/psr-complete/LPSR_80S_20MPP_ADJ.TIF. Licence: NASA/PDS public domain, credit NASA/LRO/Diviner/LOLA teams; marker M3 counts CC BY4.0 Lemelin et al. See features/NOTES.md for exact source URLs, checksums and full evidence review.

title: Steep ground
shortHelp: Yellow means take care, orange is steep, and red is over 25 degrees. Small crater bowls also get a warning. This cannot show every driving hazard.
units: 0 = no mapped warning; 1 = caution; 2 = steep; 3 = too steep to drive

notes: Source files: data-raw/source/terrain-raw/LDEM_80S_80M.JP2 (height DN x 0.5 m), data-raw/usgs-robbins-craters/lunar_crater_database_robbins_2018_bundle/data/lunar_crater_database_robbins_2018.csv (LAT_CIRC_IMG, LON_CIRC_IMG, DIAM_CIRC_IMG), and data-raw/zenodo-southpolar-small-craters/craters_psr.csv and craters_no_psr.csv (y latitude, x longitude, Diam_km). Horn 3x3 slope at native 80 m, corrected by k=1+(rho/(2*1737400))^2 exactly as the existing builder. Worst class among all native source-cell footprints overlapping each target cell; 10 <= slope < 15 deg is class 1, 15 <= slope <= 25 is class 2, >25 is class 3. Every cell intersecting a catalogued 1-3 km circular crater interior is at least class 1, a conservative bowl warning without a measured slope claim. PNG is 4096; BIN is 2048, Uint16 LE, worst of each 2x2 PNG-grid class block, 65535 outside 80 S. Classification is a project display rule, not a rover-specific mobility limit or a safe-route certification: class 0 only means no mapped warning. Horn's ~240 m baseline smooths local slopes; boulders, small craters and hazards smaller than about 80 m are unresolved. Credits: NASA/GSFC/MIT LOLA team, NASA PDS, Stuart J. Robbins / SwRI / USGS Astrogeology, Marco Figuera et al.
